author: National Geographic
description:
Class is in session and Tom Hiddleston, aka Professor Tom, shares 10 fascinating facts about the ancient Roman city of Herculaneum in this new video from National Geographic. Located even closer to Mount Vesuvius than Pompeii, Herculaneum was buried by volcanic mud after the eruption in 79 A.D., preserving homes, artifacts, and even an entire ancient library. Herculaneum offers a rare look into life in the Roman Empire before Vesuvius changed everything.

Learn more about Herculaneum in Pompeii: Out of Time with Tom Hiddleston, now streaming on Disney+ and Hulu.

author: National Geographic
description: Paid content for @waitroseandpartners. Healthy soil grows more than food; it grows the future. National Geographic photographer Matthieu Paley travels to the Waitrose Farm at the Leckford Estate to see how regenerative agriculture takes care of this precious asset through farming. As the only UK supermarket to operate its own working farm, Waitrose is committed to helping farmers transition to regenerative practices by 2030. But what exactly is regenerative farming? At its core, this technique treats soil as a living ecosystem that requires care. In the UK alone, 2 to 3 million tons of topsoil are lost every year, yet depending on the soil type, building just a single centimeter of topsoil can take 400 to 1,000 years. One key practice is the inclusion of something called an herbal ley, a field left to grow a rich mix of plants.
